Circuit (note: the whole sheet is drawn upside-down - every value label reads mirrored/rotated 180 deg - which does not affect topology; there is also a hand-drawn page-border rectangle at x~15..1010, y~285..735 that touches no component and correctly ends up on no net). A 10V source in series with a 5mH inductor and a 10MF capacitor forms the outer left loop up to a grounded top rail; a 5A current source sits in the right leg; a 2kOhm||20Ohm pair in series with a 1Ohm resistor hangs from the grounded top rail down to the bottom rail; a 10kOhm resistor links the bottom rail to the current source. 9 components, 6 nets.

  n1 = box bottom rail y~518 (x 563..684): bottom of R#1 (563,505), bottom of R#2 (684,505), top lead of R#4 (1Ohm, 646,530).

  n5 = right lead of inductor #7 (411,620) to the left terminal of V-DC #6 (433,621).

JUDGEMENT CALLS (all four CRITICAL sites read in raw pixels with inkmap, not just the rendered crop)
  S0 (630,371) deg5 - this looked like a plain X (GND column crossing the top rail), but the pixel dump settles it: the rail arrives from the left at rows 368-370 and departs to the right at rows 372-374, i.e. the drafter drew a small vertical jog and BOTH rail segments terminate on the GND column. That is two T's, not one line passing over another. JUNCTION. The crossing reading would isolate {GND, 2kOhm top, 20Ohm top} onto a net with no return path - the 2k||20 + 1Ohm string would hang off node n3 and dead-end at ground - and would leave the top rail (capacitor top + current-source top) as a separate floating net. Rule 1 and the ink both give junction.
  S4 (635,411) deg3 - clean T: the GND column descends and terminates on the box top rail, which continues left to the 2kOhm and right to the 20Ohm. JUNCTION, no real alternative.
  S8 (645,518) deg4 - T: the 1Ohm top lead rises and stops on the box bottom rail; in the pixel dump the vertical stroke extends only ~3 rows above the rail (row 515) before ending, there is no solder blob (no symmetric thickening) and no hop. The reported hop=3.6 is the mirror-written '1 Ohm' label sitting just left of the resistor, not a wire hop. JUNCTION. The crossing reading would leave the 1Ohm's top lead pointing at nothing and split the box bottom rail into two 1-terminal nets.
  S11 (638,627) deg3 - clean T: the 1Ohm bottom lead descends and terminates on the bottom rail, which continues left to the V-DC and right to the 10kOhm. JUNCTION.
  Non-critical sites left at the tracer default: S3 (569,407) box top-left corner; S6 (535,453), S9 (614,559), S15 (712,658) are handwritten value labels ('2kOhm', '1Ohm', '10kOhm') brushing wires or component boxes; S10 (537,626) is the V-DC right lead meeting the bottom rail; S12/S13/S14 (~317,655 / 306,655 / 335,659) are strokes of the '5mH' label touching the underside of the inductor. None of them change the grouping.

PORT FIXES (both were the classic 'terminal landed on the value label' failure - each produced a 1-terminal net)
  #3 Capacitor: t0 had been placed on p2@(184,522), a stroke of the mirror-written '10MF' label left of the box, giving the 1-terminal net n2. Repointed t0 to p1@(226,563), the real bottom-plate lead. t1 stays on p0@(226,504), the top-plate lead.
  #7 Inductor: t0 had been placed on p1@(305,645), a stroke of the '5mH' label written under the coil, giving the 1-terminal net n6. Repointed t0 to p3@(292,615), the real left lead - and its wire id (114) is the same wire the capacitor's bottom lead sits on, which independently confirms the reading. t1 stays on p5@(411,620), the right lead. With both fixed, old n2 and n6 collapse into one 2-terminal net, exactly as drawn.

CLASSES: all nine symbols agree with their labels (R 2kOhm, R 20Ohm, R 1Ohm, R 10kOhm, C 10MF, L 5mH, V-DC 10V with + / - inside the circle, I-DC 5A with the arrow inside the circle, GND). No reclassification.

GAP BRIDGES: 16 reported, none changes the netlist; none dropped.

UNRESOLVED: nothing.
